notes: Fifth sweep (2026-10-22-d, run head ba24972, uncommitted false): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, then the input, then references/ex_unit.md (sonnet-1 with cat in Bash, the rest with Read), matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is met in 5 of 5. Graded against the previous sweep's grades (sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/log-tests-*.json, at 3e3581d). git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows testing.md renamed to ex_unit.md, the SKILL.md trigger widened, a Formatting bullet added under "How to use this skill", and text changes to "Assert with patterns", "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else"; HEAD differs from ba24972 in no skill file.

"Assert with patterns" changed; graded against the current text. The deciding sentence is now "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier", with the example pair assert :ok == Subscriptions.subscribe(...) / assert Subscriptions.subscribe(...) == :ok. 0 of 5 put the expected value on the left (2026-10-22-c: 2 of 5, haiku-1's assert {:ok, "ch_1"} == result and sonnet-2's assert {:ok, "ch_123"} == Charger.charge(...)). opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 put the call itself on the left inside the capture (opus-1 line 43, sonnet-1 lines 36-37, sonnet-2 lines 41-42); haiku-1 and haiku-2 put the result bound by the with_log destructure on the left (haiku-1 line 44: assert result == {:error, :declined}; haiku-2 line 33), the case the new clause names. Judgment, kept from 2026-10-22-c (where it decided opus-1): binding the whole result through an exempt with_log destructure and comparing it whole with == is not "a match that binds the value and an == on it afterwards", which I read as binding part of a value; a literal reading would make the haiku tier violated. The "every match that can fail takes assert" sentence is unchanged: 0 of 5 violate; the only bare matches are with_log destructures (haiku-1 lines 39, 49, 61) or destructures of a helper returning with_log's tuple (haiku-2 lines 31, 37, 45, 51, 60, 66).

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" are unchanged since 3e3581d and clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env. opus-1 and haiku-1 use a single describe "charge/3" with three tests that each name the returned value and what was logged; the other three use describe "charge/3" plus a condition. haiku-2 uses one Payments.Gateway module answering by token; the other four use one module per outcome, nested in the test module. Every call to charge/3 runs inside capture_log/2 or with_log/2 in 5 of 5 (wrap-every-call sentence: 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-22-c); every run passes :metadata, and all but sonnet-1 pass :format (sonnet-1 keeps the default format and asserts "[warning]" and "[error]" substrings). Success absence: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 by an empty level: :warning capture; haiku-1 by refute ~r/^(warning|error) /m, which leaves out critical, alert and emergency; haiku-2 by a refute regex naming every level from warning up. No handler, StringIO device, backend or Logger.put_module_level in any run (the primary-level sentence stays unprovoked).

Outside the case's list: sonnet-1 breaks "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" at lines 63-67, where charge/3's options keyword list spans several lines inside a call whose result is matched with assert {:error, :declined} =; the rule's text changed, and the sentence that now decides it is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal ... That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." The transcript shows sonnet-1 wrote that shape itself and ran mix format, not mix format --check-formatted, after writing, so the new Formatting bullet's "a literal argument spread over several lines is a line to rewrite" did not catch it (2026-10-22-c: sonnet-1 had the same shape at three call sites). The other four ran mix format --check-formatted on the file. Wraps after =~ (haiku-1 lines 56-57, haiku-2 lines 53-54) split an operator from a regex or string literal, not a keyword list, and are not counted. Not reported, as in 2026-10-22-c: the nested gateway modules without @moduledoc false in an .exs script that builds no docs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds: every file passed every time (opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 3 tests each, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 6 each) with no compiler warning and no log line printed. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json. As in 2026-10-22-c, each file was run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous.
